01_happy_path.pdf.why: Clean invoice from a known vendor; everything reconciles.

02_po_partial_1.pdf.why: First partial delivery against PO-7781 (4,000 of 10,000).

04_po_partial_3_overrun.pdf.why: Third partial delivery. Fine on its own (2,400 < 10,000) but takes the PO to 10,900 - only visible by looking at what was already billed.

05_duplicate_reformatted.pdf.why: Same invoice as 01 re-sent with the number written differently ('INV 2026/0101'). A string-equality check would miss it.

06_resubmitted_new_number.pdf.why: Same goods and same amount as 01, new invoice number, dated 5 days later. Could be a legitimate repeat order or a double-bill - a human should decide.

07_bank_details_changed.pdf.why: Perfect invoice from a known vendor, but the IBAN is not the one on file and there is a 'new bank details' note. Classic payment-fraud pattern.

08_vat_inclusive.pdf.why: German vendor quoting gross prices (VAT included). Lines sum to the TOTAL, not the net - a naive lines==subtotal check would wrongly flag it.

09_math_error.pdf.why: Same vendor, net pricing, but the total is overstated by 100.00. Must still be caught - the tax-inclusive fallback must not make the check lenient.
